title: Privacy Matters: Vertical Federated Linear Contextual Bandits for Privacy Protected Recommendation

problem.claim: Recommendation systems must address privacy protection and compliance requirements arising from their use of personal data.

contributions.claim: The paper formulates privacy-protected recommendation as a vertical federated learning problem in which features are distributed across departments.
The paper designs an orthogonal matrix-based mask mechanism (O3M) for privacy-preserving contextual bandit learning.
The paper applies O3M to LinUCB and LinTS and instantiates two protocols for online recommendation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the proposed protocols can recover the service quality of centralized bandit algorithms while achieving satisfactory runtime efficiency, with theoretical analysis provided.
The authors report extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets showing superiority in privacy protection and recommendation performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Privacy awareness and compliance requirements create concern about personal-data use in recommendation systems, motivating privacy-protected recommendation.
The recommendation problem is formulated as vertical federated learning, and contextual bandit learning is studied in that setting.
The paper introduces the O3M encryption mechanism and uses it with LinUCB and LinTS to build online recommendation protocols.
The authors report theoretical analysis and experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets concerning service quality, runtime, privacy protection, and recommendation performance.

unknowns: The threat model and formal privacy guarantees are unspecified.
The construction and security properties of O3M are unspecified.
The exact theoretical assumptions and proof scope are unspecified.
The datasets, baselines, metrics, and experimental results are unspecified.
The meaning of perfectly recovering centralized service quality is unspecified.
